Welcome
Welcome to Swakeleys School for Girls. We are proud of our school. We are proud of our students, our staff and the opportunities we can offer to all girls, to develop their interests inside and outside of the classroom. We care deeply about each girl here and want every girl here to feel safe, enabled and proud of being their unique selves. We are rigorous in maintaining high standards for everybody, to aim to get the best from them and for them. All of this is done in a caring, nurturing way and every day we live our values:We are resilient and successfulWe are trusting and kindWe are diverse and respectfulWe hope you enjoy finding out more about our school.Kelda Stevenson Headteacher NPQH

pageCache.pageTitle: Swakeleys School for Girls - Our Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
During the academic year 2024-25 we reviewed and refined our school vision. All students, parents, staff and trustees fed into the vision which can be seen below. We wanted to make it absolutely clear what we are aiming for as a school – that we create women who are able to confidently take their place in the world, to have choices to follow their interests and passions and know that their views and opinions are important. Girls’ schools give a space for students to be fully themselves, to be known and understood and to be validated. We know the barriers that women face in society and Swakeleys School gives students a place to grow in confidence before entering that world. You will notice the values and qualities that we feel are important – from being kind and compassionate to being culturally and globally aware and having self-confidence and self-respect.
Vision for a Swakeleys School for Girls leaver
We are kind, patient and compassionate to ourselves and supportive of others. Resilience, self belief and adaptability enable us to overcome the challenges that life may throw at us. Confident in our abilities, we are able to think critically and with curiosity about the world around us. We are culturally and globally aware, accepting, open-minded and inclusive. We develop strong and trusting relationships. Upon leaving Swakeleys we enjoy academic and personal success because we have worked hard and this gives us self-confidence and self-respect. We are honest, optimistic and ambitious for our future – whatever that may hold
We also spent time as a school community in 2024-25 to consider what we feel to be important – our school values. Again, everyone involved in our school community was invited to contribute. We decided on three value statements which are what we stand for as a school. The value statements are:
We are resilient and successful We are trusting and kind We are diverse and respectful
Having clarity on our school values helps all of us to understand how we should act and behave and helps us to know right from wrong. We talk about our values a lot at Swakeleys. It is who we are and what we stand for. We asked Swakeleys students to clarify what our values really mean. Please see below what they said:
Resilient
We try hard and we keep trying. We develop our character through learning, clubs, activities and leadership opportunities. We are adaptable. We are open to advice and support. We value and work at our mental and physical health. We understand that life will bring challenges and that we can develop the skills to meet them. We are optimistic.
Successful
We strive for excellence in everything that we do. We work hard in every lesson and set high expectations for ourselves. We aim for small improvements every day. We believe in ourselves and set personal goals. We think critically. We are present and punctual. We act on academic advice. We learn and refine new skills. We think and plan ahead. We celebrate progress, perseverance and hard work. We show commitment to learning in the classroom and beyond. We are ambitious.
Trusting
We believe in our school values. We work towards common goals. We understand that a school is made of the people in it and their actions. We do what we know is right. We have identified adults that we can confide in. We work hard to develop strong relationships. We listen to the ideas and opinions of others. We raise concerns using the structures and policies of our school. We listen actively. We explain our choices and decisions. We feel safe on our school site. We are consistent and clear.
Kind
We support and encourage others and celebrate their success. We are friendly and welcoming. We keep hands and hurtful comments to ourselves in the real world and in the virtual world. We are compassionate in our thoughts and in our actions. We have patience. We care about other people and our society. We give our time in the service of others. We are charitable. We forgive and move on.
Diverse
We promote equality and celebrate the unique qualities of all individuals. We make everybody feel valued. We take action against discrimination through our policies. We celebrate our difference and our unique qualities. We are globally and culturally aware. We are open minded and accepting. We grow and learn from our diversity. We are open to enriching ourselves through learning from each other.
Respectful
We stand together against prejudice, racism and intolerance. We understand and follow laws and rules. We listen in silence while others speak. We follow instructions at the first time of asking. We are polite and courteous in our speech and in our actions. We understand what good manners are and demonstrate them. We say please and thank you. We understand our own value, and that of people around us. We accept responsibility for our words and what we do. We consider the impact of our actions on our community and environment. We look after property and premises. We understand that we are all important.
At Swakeleys we support our students to become confident women who are empowered to manage the challenges that they can experience at different stages of life.
There is no one type of girl welcome here – Swakeleys is for all girls and the girls tell us how safe they feel at school – safe to be themselves.
Diary Dates

pageCache.text:
Careers Guidance
Careers provision at Swakeleys School for Girls and Sixth Form
Careers Staff
To contact the above please use the school email address: office@swakeleys.org.uk and mark in the subject who it is for the attention of.
The Careers team at Swakeleys School for Girls provides information, advice and guidance to students so they can develop the skills needed for a working life. This supports the more general careers education students receive in subject lessons, Form Group tutorials, assemblies and general careers events. Careers guidance and education is delivered in all Key Stages as an integral part of the PSHCE programme. In sixth form, the careers guidance is expertly supported by external advisors who provide bespoke guidance on the UCAS process to students and parents.
From Year 8 onwards, they are given progressive support to reflect on career choices, to prepare for work experience and to research career opportunities. For our Year 11 students we provide particularly intensive support as they make important decisions about which Post-16 pathway to follow: academic A Levels; vocational BTECs; or workplace Apprenticeships.
Swakeleys School for Girls and Sixth Form works in partnership with Learning to Work and the Education Development Trust (EDT) to employ independent careers advisors who deliver impartial careers advice and guidance to learners and parents / carers of pupils in the school. Every student from Years 7 to 13 will have access to a careers interview which is individually tailored to their particular needs. Personalised action plans are developed with the student during the meeting and their execution is monitored by the student’s Form Tutor and via a follow up careers meeting should this be required.
Miss Anoosh Salar is available for 1-1 appointments each Monday & Tuesday from 9.00am – 3.20pm, Room A171
A careers advisor is present at our Year 11 Parents Evening and on GCSE / A-level Results Day to help and guide students in making informed choices about their future.
Swakeleys School for Girls and Sixth Form is keen to promote the STEM agenda and we are committed to promoting careers in science, technology, engineering and maths. Numerous events, integrated into the careers programme offers providers from different industries to share their knowledge and experience of their field of work.
At Swakeleys School, we aim to give students a broad and varied experience of the world of work from Key Stage 3 onwards. Through multiple opportunities across the curriculum and our wider careers programme, students are introduced to a diverse range of workplaces, industries, occupations and career pathways.
This includes visits to different workplace environments, such as the Year 7 Virus Factory Trip, where students explore STEM, science and research careers. In Year 8 we take students to the Hilton Hotel, where they gain an insight into the wide range of careers within the hospitality industry. Departments areas also provide curriculum-linked opportunities that connect students' subjects to the world of work. In recent years, our students have benefited from a wide range of workplace and career-related visits, including Warner Bros. Studio Tour London – The Making of Harry Potter, where students explore careers in set design, film and movie make-up; Sky Studios, providing an insight into careers in Media; Bosch UK Headquarters, linking Geography to the world of work; the Houses of Parliament, helping students explore careers connected to History, politics and public life; and Behind the Stage theatre experiences, introducing students to the diverse range of careers within the Performing Arts.
Through these multiple encounters with workplaces, employees and different industries throughout Key Stage 3, we aim to broaden students’ horizons and raise their awareness of the diverse range of careers available to them. These experiences enable students to see how their learning in the classroom connects to the world beyond school, while helping them to develop a better understanding of different workplaces, roles and career pathways. This early and varied exposure provides a strong foundation for the more established week long Year 10 Work Shadowing Programme. We work in partnership with our families, local schools, libraries and local businesses to source suitable placements as part of the programme. Completing the workshadowing programme is hugely valuable and students often refer to the experience and skills they have developed through their work placements in future job application or in their UCAS personal statements.
Throughout the year, we engage in events offered by companies and external agencies to maximise our students exposure to the world of work. Please click below to find the following useful careers documents.
Measuring the impact of our careers programme
We use a wide range of evaluation tools to measure the success of our careers programme. These include: Compass+ evaluation tool which assesses ongoing progress against Gatsby benchmarks. We do a full evaluation of our Careers Fair and Work Shadowing programme using Google Forms to obtain pupil feedback. The options process is also fully reviewed each year and adaptions made including pupil and parental feedback. Our Careers Advisor continually reviews the effectiveness of the 1-2-1 guidance interviews on a termly basis including pupil engagement. All career related trips are also reviewed in terms of pupil enjoyment and value. Our evaluations also look at a range of evidence including attainment, progress, option numbers, destination data and feedback.

Parent Pay
ParentPay – this is our new online payment service.
We are pleased to announce that we are now accepting payments online for items such as dinner money, school trips and uniform. Using a secure website called ParentPay you can pay online using your credit or debit card. ParentPay will be our preferred method of making payments to school.
We are hoping that everyone will benefit from our new payment facility. ParentPay is easy-to-use and offers you the freedom to make online payments whenever and wherever you like, 24/7 – safe in the knowledge that the technology used is of the highest internet security available and that funds will reach school safely. Parents all now have a secure online account, activated using a unique username and password; making a payment using your credit or debit card is straightforward and ParentPay holds an electronic record of all payments for you to view at a later date. When you make a payment, an e-mail confirmation is sent to you, giving you reassurance that the transaction has been successful.
In addition, ParentPay offers you the ability to set automated email/SMS reminders ensuring you never miss a payment and helping you keep your child’s school meal account in credit at all times. The more parents that use ParentPay, the greater the benefit is to the school. You can help us reduce workloads for all staff, creating more time to lend to educational support and the smooth running of the school. It also ensures that all financial transactions are safe and secure.
Getting started with ParentPay
Once set up, we will send you an account activation username and password. Once you receive these:
Please be assured that ParentPay offers the highest security available and no card details are stored on the system or are accessible by the school or ParentPay. If you have any questions, please contact the school Finance Office.
We look forward to your support in using ParentPay as it will help us further support teaching and learning by reducing the burden of income collection in the classrooms and school office.
Diary Dates

REMOTE LEARNING
At Swakeleys School for Girls, we use Google Classroom as our main platform for remote learning.
If students need to learn from home (for example due to school closure), all lesson materials and instructions will be posted on Google Classroom for each subject.
When appropriate and where possible, teachers will deliver live lessons to ensure continuity of learning and provide opportunities for interaction and feedback.
This approach means that students can follow the planned curriculum and continue to make progress even when they cannot attend school in person.

Swakeleys School for Girls - Super Curricular Activities
pageCache.text:
Super Curricular Activities
Alongside specific subject studies all students in Swakeleys Sixth Form are expected to spend at least 1 hour per week engaged in Super-Curricular activities.
What is it?Super-curricular is different from extra-curricular. Extra-curricular activities are those outside of a student’s chosen topic, and unrelated to their studies, whereas super-curricular activities take the subjects they study further, beyond what they have learnt at school or college.
Why is it important? Highly selective universities explain that Super-curricular activities can help a student make a competitive application, and prepare them for a challenging academic environment. Super-curricular participation can enhance a personal statement, and give a student a greater confidence in their subject choice. They can demonstrate that a student is serious about their area of study, and give them a wealth of ideas to draw upon in discussions if they are invited to interview.
Beyond that it’s likely that students will develop new ideas and opinions, critical thinking and analytical skills, and an ability to understand new information from different sources – this is all great preparation for future success
What is a super curricular activity?
We have an extensive selection of books and journals in the Sixth form LRC to support students with accessing wider reading.
Students have access to a Swakeleys Super Curricular website to help them in accessing these opportunities.
This can be accessed here: https://sites.google.com/swakeleys.org.uk/supercurricular

Curriculum Guide: Year 10
Year 10 students study the following core subjects; English, English Literature, maths, science (trilogy worth 2 GCSEs), RE and a Language or Humanity (history or geography). They also study two additional GCSE option choices and have core PE and PSHCE as part of their non-examined core curriculum. The following provides families and students with guidance on what the full academic year of learning looks like for each subject. It outlines what Year 10 students will be taught, the type of assessment that students will experience and any resources that they will need.
Year 10 also have an internal exam period of two weeks where full mock exams are sat, as they will be at the end of Year 11. These fall in Summer 1 and are to give students a real experience of what final GCSE exams will be like when the time comes!
